comparison: Both strongly support the antibacterial activity of LDs and histones (C15, C18-C22). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple assays with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers describe this as a 'remarkable new finding' with 'outstanding' results, accepting the in vitro antibacterial activity data without critique.

Both address Jabba mutant phenotypes and histone accumulation (C29-C33). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by multiple complementary approaches with two independent alleles. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, recommending testing Jabba in another mutant background to exclude possible background effects, despite acknowledging the finding allowed a direct test.

Both support bacterial growth differences between wild-type and Jabba mutants (C4, C5, C39-C49). OpenEval notes the dramatic contrast but acknowledges uncertainty in absolute numbers from limited field quantification. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'a large difference in bacterial growth was observed' and describe results as 'outstanding,' though request more quantitative assessment.

Perfect agreement on survival data (C6, C50-C53). Both strongly support the fourfold survival difference across multiple bacterial species. OpenEval emphasizes statistical robustness and biological significance. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'four to five fold difference in embryo survival' as part of the core demonstration of the antibacterial defense system.

Perfect agreement on control observations (C36-C38). Both support these claims establishing that Jabba mutation specifically affects bacterial defense rather than general viability. OpenEval notes importance for establishing specificity. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of critique.

Both address adult fly experiments (C55-C63) but with different levels of confidence. OpenEval supports the claims while acknowledging authors' statement that investigation is 'limited' and more work remains. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, characterizing results as done 'in a limited way' and suggesting evidence is preliminary or incomplete.

Perfect agreement on regulated histone release mechanism (C2, C64-C72, C97). Both support the dose-dependent histone release in response to LPS and LTA. OpenEval emphasizes dose-response relationship and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of the 'remarkable new finding' without specific critique.

Both address histone characterization (C23, C24, C27). OpenEval supports claims while noting mass spectrometry is 'mostly qualitative,' introducing some uncertainty. Peer reviewers do not specifically discuss these details, suggesting implicit acceptance as supporting data without controversy.

Both address mammalian LD histone findings (C75-C79) but diverge on additional claims. OpenEval supports histone H1 on mammalian LDs while noting species-specific differences. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about mammalian experiments (C75-C79, C81-C83), noting issues with LPS infection measurement and recommending to 'tone down this section' as experiments are 'rather limited, if provocative.'

OpenEval addresses LPS-induced H1 increase (C81-C83) as SUPPORTED with modest fold-change. Peer reviewers group this with broader mammalian experiments (R7) and rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about measuring LPS infection efficiency and characterizing experiments as limited.

Major disagreement on speculative/mechanistic claims (C84-C86, C88, C90, C96, C98-C99, C102, C104-C105). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are largely speculative and require additional experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, characterizing overall work as 'remarkable' with 'outstanding' results, not challenging core mechanistic interpretation despite requesting acknowledgment of limitations.

OpenEval identifies extensive literature-based claims (C7-C14, C16-C17, C25-C26, C35, C66-C68, C73-C74, C80, C89, C91-C95, C100, C106) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than literature citations.

OpenEval supports in vitro assay claims (C3, C27, C101, C103) demonstrating intrinsic antibacterial properties of histones and charge-sensitivity of binding. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C27 appears in peer R8 as implicitly accepted supporting data.
